artboards.title: B · A node as the learner reads it
C · Entering from a Labs decision

annotations.text:
B2 — the front door is a PATH, not a graph.

The zoom control works: click it. Three positions, collapsing rather than hiding — at 'spine' the 47 other nodes are folded into the +N chips, so you can see more exists without facing it.

Metacademy and Khan's Knowledge Map both put the graph on the front door. Both are gone.

A — the highest-risk screen in the project.

Measured finding: teacher-revised AI items carry MORE flaws than teacher-only ones. Automation bias, visible as low interaction density.

So Approve is two steps away on purpose: mark every unsourced assertion, then answer the node's own checks. The claim is already locked — it gates everything else.

B — one node, all its holes rendered.

Green band = the per-track FRAMING hole, the escape from the reusability paradox. Red band = the misconception. The worked example is real and executable; the check has a discriminating answer.

Footer discloses AI-drafted / human-approved, per the MIT report.

C — the forcing function no competitor has.

Left is Mendel's tier-3 decision with its rule, premise and citation. Right is Code, entered FROM it.

Note what the drawer leads with: what you need to judge the decision yourself. The short answer is present but deliberately last and framed as the rule's reasoning — that is the cognitive-surrender guard.
